keyFinding: 6 of 11 evidence items are SELF_BUILDING_ONLY. Only 2 are from non-Factory benchmarks. No large-project external benchmark evidence exists. Multi-agent value for large projects remains UNPROVEN but PLAUSIBLE.

evidenceItems.observedBenefit: Parallel package creation reduced wall-clock time vs sequential Main Agent
evidenceItems.failureCaveat: Cross-worker deps limited to 30 (contractual + code edges). No large-project benchmark comparison.
evidenceItems.relevanceToLargeProject: MODERATE: Shows multi-agent can work, but only in Factory self-building context. Not proven in external large project.
evidenceItems.claimedCapability: 6 builders + integrator delivering 90 source files with 1121 exports

evidenceItems.observedBenefit: Automatic agent registration and progress event recording
evidenceItems.failureCaveat: No spawn failure detection in factoryctl verify
evidenceItems.observedCost: Not on PATH; requires explicit repo-local invocation
evidenceItems.relevanceToLargeProject: HIGH: Agent tracking infrastructure is essential for large-project multi-agent
evidenceItems.claimedCapability: Native agent registry and progress tracking via repo-local scripts

evidenceItems.observedBenefit: 34 quarantined files identified as contaminated; 3 replacement agents spawned
evidenceItems.failureCaveat: Contamination detected only after closure claim, not prevented upfront
evidenceItems.observedCost: Full P2 repair phase needed after false closure in P1
evidenceItems.relevanceToLargeProject: CRITICAL: Main Agent fallback is the #1 risk for multi-agent in large projects
evidenceItems.claimedCapability: Detection and repair of Main Agent undeclared fallback writing worker scope

evidenceItems.observedBenefit: Identified and closed unsafe stale agents; archived historical agents
evidenceItems.failureCaveat: Stale agent detection is post-hoc, not real-time
evidenceItems.observedCost: Manual investigation required; no automatic stale detection in factoryctl
evidenceItems.relevanceToLargeProject: HIGH: Large projects will accumulate many agents; lifecycle management is essential
evidenceItems.claimedCapability: Classification of 28 open agents, 26 stale, with cleanup actions

evidenceItems.observedBenefit: Contract-driven scope isolation and dependency management
evidenceItems.failureCaveat: Contract CI enforcement not fully automated; dependency extraction missed contract-declared deps
evidenceItems.observedCost: Contracts were DRY23-A generated, not natively created by agents at spawn time
evidenceItems.relevanceToLargeProject: CRITICAL: Worker contracts are the foundation of multi-agent scope isolation
evidenceItems.claimedCapability: 25 worker contracts with owned scopes, allowed/forbidden imports, dependency declarations

evidenceItems.failureCaveat: Project too small for multi-agent benefit. 10 roles for a small team app is excessive overhead.
evidenceItems.observedCost: 10-role model was overkill for TeamFlow scale; did not beat Factory Lite
evidenceItems.relevanceToLargeProject: LOW: Evidence from small project; not predictive of large-project behavior
evidenceItems.claimedCapability: Simulated role-based agents (Architect, Builder, Reviewer) in a small project

evidenceItems.observedBenefit: Some role separation benefits observed but insufficient to overcome overhead
evidenceItems.failureCaveat: EVAL-13 INCONCLUSIVE: Role-Agent did not clearly beat Factory Lite. But project was medium scale.
evidenceItems.observedCost: Higher agent overhead; slower completion; more integration defects
evidenceItems.relevanceToLargeProject: MODERATE: Shows role-agent overhead can dominate at medium scale, but doesn't answer for large scale
evidenceItems.claimedCapability: Role-based agents vs Factory Lite in TeamFlow project

evidenceItems.observedBenefit: Demonstrated multi-agent can prevent Codex from simplifying complex tasks
evidenceItems.failureCaveat: Only tested in Factory self-building; not validated against external large project
evidenceItems.observedCost: Cross-worker deps limited; 12 negatives detected structural limitations
evidenceItems.relevanceToLargeProject: HIGH: Complexity preservation is exactly what large projects need from multi-agent
evidenceItems.claimedCapability: 7 agents, 4 real spawned builders, fork_context:false, 64 TypeScript files, 484 exports

evidenceItems.observedBenefit: Conceptual exploration of agent operating system capabilities
evidenceItems.failureCaveat: No implementation, no evidence. Pure design hypothesis.
evidenceItems.observedCost: None implemented; all deferred to future versions
evidenceItems.relevanceToLargeProject: LOW: Deferred capabilities with no evidence
evidenceItems.claimedCapability: Context OS, MCP Memory, Automation Watcher, Session Controller as potential agent infrastructure

evidenceItems.observedBenefit: Comprehensive role taxonomy for design reference
evidenceItems.failureCaveat: Too many roles created excessive overhead and integration complexity for available evidence scale
evidenceItems.observedCost: Overkill for Factory self-building; did not beat Factory Lite in EVAL-13
evidenceItems.relevanceToLargeProject: MODERATE: Role taxonomy is useful reference; 10 roles as default is rejected
evidenceItems.claimedCapability: Full 10-role organizational model (Founder, CTO, Architect, PM, Builder, Integrator, Verifier, Auditor, DevOps, Knowledge Mgmt)
